mods.description: Bounded-distribution random teleport. NeoForge platform adapter (in-scope per ADR-033).

releases.notes:
### Added

- **Tune background cache refill automatically from server headroom and player demand (`autoTune`, [ADR-087](https://github.com/DailyStruggle/RTP/tree/V3/docs/adr/ADR-087-adaptive-compute-governor.md), [ADR-123](https://github.com/DailyStruggle/RTP/tree/V3/docs/adr/ADR-123-folia-tick-region-allocation.md), [ADR-124](https://github.com/DailyStruggle/RTP/tree/V3/docs/adr/ADR-124-consumer-attribution-for-background-refill.md)).** `advanced/performance.yml` ships `autoTune: true`. While players teleport and the server has spare tick time, CPU and memory, regions refill on every tick within `asyncAllottedTime`, `syncAllottedTime` and `activeChunkCap` instead of waiting for `period`. When tick time, CPU, chunk-load latency or tenured heap usage rises, or when caches are already full, background refill scales down before `minTPS`, `maxMSPT` or `maxHeapPercent` trips, while players waiting for a teleport keep the full configured budgets; constrained refill is shared across regions by distinct active players (`ADR-124`), and on Folia tick-region shares are probed per cell group and background work prefers tick regions with headroom and fewer players up to a 60 s or 8-deferral aging bound (`ADR-123`). `/rtp info` shows effective budgets, per-region refill shares and top consumers, and `/rtp test` includes the `compute-governor` check for reduced or floor-held budgets and stale metrics; setting `autoTune: false` uses the fixed values and refills once per `period`.

- **Action and Claim addons report setup health through BIT ([ADR-121](https://github.com/DailyStruggle/RTP/tree/V3/docs/adr/ADR-121-built-in-test-for-configuration-and-the-action-engine.md)).** `/rtp test action-setup` identifies rejected definitions, command or trigger registration failures, missing batch scheduling and name collisions. On Bukkit-family servers, `/rtp test claim-integrations` reports disabled, absent, late-enabled and incompatible claim integrations. Each addon publishes a separate code catalog and stable identity lock; first-boot severity overrides for addon codes take effect after addon registration.

- **Refuse steep landing spots ([ADR-119](https://github.com/DailyStruggle/RTP/tree/V3/docs/adr/ADR-119-slope-detection-and-elevation-memory.md)).** `linear` and `jump` verts accept two new optional keys. `maxSlope` is the largest floor-height step, in blocks, allowed between the landing spot and the ground `slopeRadius` blocks away (default `2`, range `1`-`8`) to the north, south, east and west. Spots on cliff edges or steep hillsides are skipped and the search moves on to the next spot. The check follows the floor the player would stand on, so it also works in caves and the Nether. Regions without `maxSlope` behave as before and keep their saved region data. Setting or changing either key rebuilds that region's saved data once. Steep worlds with a low `maxSlope` reject more chunks. Not available on `fixed`, which places players in mid-air.

releases.notes:
> **Upgrade note.** `rtp.servers.*` now defaults to `true` instead of `op`, so in network mode every player can reach open cross-server regions; restrict with negative permissions if you relied on the old default. `CIRCLE` and `SQUARE` now use new selection engines that ignore `weight`; use `CIRCLE_DEPRECATED_PURE_SPIRAL` or `SQUARE_DEPRECATED_PURE_SPIRAL` to keep the 3.2.1 behavior. Region shapes now default to `mode: REROLL` instead of `ACCUMULATE`; files that set `mode` keep their value. In `config.yml`, `defaults.shape.uniquePlacements` now defaults to `"auto"` (a radius matching the view distance) instead of `0`, and `defaults.spatialResolution` to `"auto"` (scaled to the region's size) instead of `3`; set `0` and `3` to keep the 3.2.1 values. Both jars now load on Minecraft 1.18 or newer with Java 17 or newer; the Lite jar no longer loads on 1.13 - 1.17. Folia is supported only from 1.21.11; older Folia still loads the jar but is no longer supported. Saved memory and region cache files from 3.2.1 still load, but RTP rewrites them in a new format at the next save or shutdown, and 3.2.1 can't read that format, so back up `plugins/RTP/` if you may need to roll back.

### Added

- **Runs on Spigot and Paper 1.18 - 1.20.6, and on Java 17 ([ADR-113](https://github.com/DailyStruggle/RTP/tree/V3/docs/adr/ADR-113-java-17-baseline-and-26x-support-boundary.md)).** The full jar now loads on Spigot and Paper 1.18 through 1.20.6, and Fabric 1.20.1 servers can run it on Java 17. These older versions are best-effort and are not covered by automated tests. NeoForge still needs 1.21.1 or newer, and Fabric 1.20.2 - 1.20.6 is not supported. Folia is supported from 1.21.11: it is experimental and only its current builds are maintained, so older Folia builds are not supported and can crash on their own. Bug reports are accepted for Minecraft 1.21.11 through the latest release; the per-version status is in the [support matrix](https://github.com/DailyStruggle/RTP/blob/V3/docs/dev/SUPPORT_MATRIX.md).

- **Tag exclusions in `safety.yml` (ADR-017).** Remove entries from a block tag instead of listing every variant by hand, e.g. `#minecraft:slabs - OAK_SLAB`.

- **Actions.** Script multi-step teleports in YAML: what happens before, during and after the teleport, what to do on failure or timeout, and conditions that must pass first (permission, balance, cooldown, world, biome, time, server load and more). Destinations can be anchored to a player, a claim, a faction or a world center, and teams can be placed together. Walk-in triggers start an action when a player enters a zone. Commands: `/rtp action` (`rtp.action`; `/rtp trigger` and `/rtp run` are other names for it), `/rtp action cancel` (`rtp.action.cancel`) and `/rtp back` (`rtp.back`). The bundled action addon ships ready-made modes such as arena, KOTH, scatter and teams.

- **Web config editor (`/rtp editor`).** Edit RTP's configs in a browser and apply the changes back to the server. Permission: `rtp.editor`. The region map shows the land of every loaded world, including the nether and the end, and a region's world can be picked from the worlds the server detected. Passwords, tokens and other secrets are redacted before anything leaves the server and are never overwritten by the editor. Only config files inside the plugin folder can be written, and a browser must be trusted before it can apply changes (revoke with `/rtp editor untrust`; optional expiry with `editor.trust.maxAgeDays` in `advanced/network.yml`).

# RTP v3 — Foundations (beta.1)

The first beta of the v3 line. This release is the **foundation** the rest of v3 builds on: a stable public `rtp-api`, versioned platform submodules, SQL-backed persistence, lock-free pre-generation, and a hardened safety pipeline. Bukkit, Paper, and Folia are production-ready on Java 21+ for Minecraft 1.20.x / 1.21.x / 26.1.

> ⚠️ **Major release — breaking `rtp-api` changes.** See [MIGRATION.md](https://github.com/DailyStruggle/RTP/blob/master/docs/admin/MIGRATION.md#upgrading-to-300-beta) before upgrading from 2.x.

---

## Highlights

1. **Versioned platform submodules** — compile-time NMS separation via a `common` module plus per-version submodules for Spigot, Paper, and Folia (ADR-010).
2. **Stable public `rtp-api`** — broadened addon surface; no more reflection into internals (ADR-011).
3. **Multi-backend persistence** — flat-file sector cache replaced by SQL-backed storage: H2 (default), SQLite, MySQL, PostgreSQL, plus Redis caching and YAML fallback (ADR-002).
4. **Per-platform scheduling pipelines** — Folia regional-thread scheduling, Paper native async chunk loading (PaperLib removed), Spigot Bukkit scheduler (ADR-004–006).
5. **Lock-free location buffer + state-based tasks** — `LockFreeLocationBuffer` decouples pre-generation from dispatch; explicit task states enable pause/resume/cancel and concurrent region fills.
6. **`ChunkReservation` lifecycle** — `AutoCloseable` abstraction eliminates the 2.x ticket leak (ADR-012).
7. **Anvil read-only pre-filter** — off-tick safety probing of unloaded chunks on Spigot via direct `.mca` reads (ADR-016). Measured 16–20× speedup vs. full chunk load.
8. **Claim integrations folded into the plugin** — Factions, GriefDefender, GriefPrevention, HuskTowns, Lands, RedProtect, TownyAdvanced, WorldGuard now ship in-box (ADR-019).
9. **Brigadier bridge** for Paper/Folia tab-completion (ADR-014).
10. **Documentation & governance overhaul** — full REQ-ID requirements, traceability matrix, ADRs, admin runbook, hazard catalog, migration guide.

---

## Supported scope (beta)

**In scope and supported:**
- Spigot, Paper, Folia on MC 1.20.x / 1.21.x / 26.1, Java 21+
- H2 (default) and SQLite persistence
- Public `rtp-api` types
- Claim integrations (8 plugins)
- Anvil pre-filter (Spigot)
- Brigadier bridge (Paper/Folia)

**Out of scope — do not file as bugs:**
- **Fabric** — present in source, **not functional yet**. Do not deploy on Fabric. Targeted for `3.0.0` final.
- **Forge / NeoForge** — no native adapter. Use Arclight/Mohist with the Spigot/Paper build.
- **Multi-server / proxy mode** (Velocity, BungeeCord) — design only.
- **MySQL / PostgreSQL / Redis / YAML accessors** — experimental; use H2 or SQLite in production.
- **`RTPEconomy` API** and **`/rtp config` command** — experimental; signatures may change before final.
- **Legacy MC < 1.20 / Java < 21** — unsupported (ADR-021).

---

## Known issues

- Fabric adapter is non-functional (see above).
- `safety.yml` and biome-filter edits do not invalidate the persisted shape cache. Workaround: `/rtp scan reset <region>` after changing safety predicates.
- Tag-grammar tokens in `safety.yml` (e.g. `#minecraft:flowers`) are accepted but inert — use explicit material names for now.
- **Pre-release cache invalidation:** legacy 2.x `.bin` files and any pre-`3.0.0-beta.1` `rtp_cached_locations` rows are abandoned by the new hash-keyed naming scheme. Expect a one-time re-scan on first launch.
- **Default change:** `safety.yml` now ships `platformRadius: -1` (emergency platform disabled). Set `platformRadius: 0` or higher to restore legacy 2.x behaviour.

---

## Upgrading from 2.x

1. **Back up your world and `plugins/RTP/` folder.**
2. Read [MIGRATION.md](https://github.com/DailyStruggle/RTP/blob/master/docs/admin/MIGRATION.md#upgrading-to-300-beta).
3. Ensure Java 21+ and a supported platform version.
4. Drop in the new jar; expect a one-time region re-scan.
